text: The asphalt paving up to the Mapleton gates
why: The asphalt paving leading up to the Mapleton gates is described in ¶124.

text: The gates of the Mapleton stables
why: The gates of the Mapleton stables are named in ¶124.
¶124 says a groom ran out from the gates.

text: Thursday evening, at the gates of the Mapleton stables
why: They set out Thursday morning and reached Tavistock in the evening, and the walk takes place before dark, so Thursday evening follows directly.

text: When the same tracks came back to the Mapleton gates
why: The return tracks ending at the Mapleton gates are described in ¶122-124.

text: Did Silas Brown and the Mapleton people have a hand in the affair? — he found the horse loose and took it in
id: q.brown_part=he found the horse loose and took it in
why: The horse's lone track, then a man's track beside it, ending at Mapleton, gives a reader reason to suspect that Mapleton's trainer took in the loose horse. Brown has already been named as a suspect.

text: Who was the man whose track joined the horse's near Mapleton? — someone from the Mapleton stables
why: The man's track ends at the Mapleton gates, so it is a natural possibility that he came from Mapleton.
